overview.title: About the science unit
overview.description: Scientific activity connects education, clinical practice, and research in one ecosystem.
overview.p1: The science unit at Saribekyan International Medical University organizes and coordinates university research, scientific projects, and dissemination of results. Activity includes faculty, postgraduate researchers, and students.
overview.p2: Priority areas include biomedical and clinical research, public health, and education science aimed at improving medical education quality.

research.title: Scientific research
research.description: Scientific activity is an integral part of the university’s educational process at SIMU. University specialists and students take part in a wide range of biomedical research projects, in collaboration with leading hospitals and research centres in Armenia and abroad. Scientific articles and conference materials are published in reputable local and international handbooks and journals, covering fundamental, clinical, and case studies. The university also publishes teaching handbooks and organizes international scientific events.

ugs.title: SSS
ugs.p1: The Student Scientific Society is active at the university. It organizes university scientific events and publishes articles and conference materials in reputable local and international journals and handbooks.
ugs.p2: Since 2022, a student facilitator system has also been introduced. It is innovative in nature and has created greater opportunities to involve students in scientific work.

research.title: SSS Health-Wise
research.description: Within this project, SIMU students and specialists produce popular-science videos based on small research projects.

events.title: SSS Debate Club
events.description: The project hosts student scientific debates in a format developed by the SIMU Student Scientific Society.

mentoring.title: SSS “A-Eyes” startup
mentoring.description: This student project, created in 2023, develops systems that support people with visual impairments. With the university’s support, the team has taken part in and been presented at many international and local scientific and student platforms.
